clue.text: Most hockey balls become very dense objects

indicators.note: become signals the letters turn into something else, a rearrangement of the pool
most of the word hockey means all of it except its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of hockey, dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that most hockey balls end up far too heavy and solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' trims the last letter from hockey, leaving HOCKE; 'become' rearranges HOCKE with BALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapsed stars of enormous density whose gravity traps even light are the astronomer's ultimate dense objects.

clue.text: Stood and gave birth

definitions.meaning: to have stood something is to have tolerated or endured it
past tense of the verb meaning to carry and deliver a child

explanation.surface: Someone stood up and then had a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb that means both tolerate and bring forth young covers each sense.

clue.text: Academy has large study featuring rising tribal star

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: featuring means the study has another piece included within it

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Arab used adjectively, of the desert peoples and their tribes

explanation.surface: A learned body with a big study containing some upstart tribal celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the tribal word upwards, as this is a down clue; 'featuring' holds it inside the study. 'star' pretends to be a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright orange giant marking the eye of Taurus is a named star.

clue.text: Money found in Camden or Kensington to be given back

indicators.note: given back says the letters found are read in the opposite direction
found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Cash discovered in two London districts must be returned to its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' picks ENORK from camdEN OR Kensington; 'to be given back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the currency unit of Denmark and Norway, a kind of money.

clue.text: Not against a hint of salt in savoury recipe that contains bones

indicators.note: a recipe mixes ingredients, so it signals the letters are rearranged
not says the following letter is to be left out of the word nearby

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: a hint of something is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cookery note: go easy on the salt in a savoury dish made with bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not against' removes V from SAVOURY leaving SAOURY; 'a hint of' gives S; 'recipe' rearranges the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A container or vault in which the bones of the dead are kept, so a thing holding skeletal remains.

clue.text: Plead with nurse to carry out doctor's orders

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
to give the care a doctor prescribes is to treat a patient

explanation.surface: Begging a nurse to follow the doctor's instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech or beg someone earnestly is to plead with them; a synonym.

clue.text: Write note about lecturer's shock

indicators.note: about means the jotting surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to jot something down is to write a quick note

explanation.surface: Taking down notes on the surprise a lecturer had.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden jerk or a startling surprise; a synonym of shock.

clue.text: Gold particle hunter

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
an ion is a charged atomic particle

explanation.surface: A prospector after a fleck of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gold hunter; the hunter is the mythical one, now a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant hunter of Greek myth, placed in the sky as a constellation, fits the puzzle's astronomy theme.

clue.text: Races across fashionable street with intro for short piece of music

indicators.note: across means the races stretch over the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: the TT, the Tourist Trophy, is a series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
hep is old slang for stylish or in the know
a lane is a narrow street

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Speeding over a trendy road, with a little opening for a short musical item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts the fashionable street inside the races; 'intro for' takes S from 'short', which pretends to qualify the music although Holst's suite is long.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's orchestral suite depicting the planets of the solar system is a celebrated work of music.

clue.text: Going on and off loudly using tongue

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loudly
licking is applying the tongue to something

explanation.surface: Something noisy happening with a tongue, like a cat lapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A light switched repeatedly up and down is being turned on and off, a verb in the same continuous form.

clue.text: Republican Bill Moon seen in sort of telescope

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A US Republican named Bill Moon is observed through some kind of telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Moon' reads as a person's name but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish that collects radio waves from space is a kind of telescope used by astronomers.

clue.text: Excellent archer in place one is going round

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the place

parts.note: a site is a place or location
A is a top grade, so excellent
William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A first-rate archer standing at a spot where something circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' gives A, as a top mark; 'archer' is William Tell of Swiss legend. 'one is going round' sounds like a person, but it is an orbiting body.
explanation.definitionFit: A body that orbits a planet travels round and round it, so something that circles.

clue.text: Deny scandal of sailor from Tyneside?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
Tyneside, round Newcastle, lies in the north-east of England, NE
-gate is the suffix tacked onto scandals since Watergate

explanation.surface: Refusing to admit a scandal about a seaman from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse oneself something is to deny it; a formal synonym.

clue.text: Part of an ear found in oilcan alarming

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: Spotting something in an ear that sets off alarm, as if an oil can had got in.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear canal is the tube leading in to the eardrum, a part of the ear.

clue.text: Welsh politician low on gas receives note from diplomat

parts.note: AM, Assembly Member, was the title of a member of the Welsh Assembly
bass means low in pitch

indicators.note: receives means the gas takes the note inside it

parts.note: Ar is the chemical symbol for the gas argon
do, or doh, is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician short of fuel gets a note from an envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts the note inside the gas symbol. 'low on gas' looks like being short of fuel, but 'low' is a pitch and 'on' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior envoy representing a country abroad is a diplomat; the answer is an example.

clue.text: Copper intervenes amid drunken element

indicators.note: something that intervenes amid others comes between them, going inside

parts.note: merry is a mild word for tipsy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer steps into the middle of a drunken brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' poses as a police officer but is the chemical symbol CU, which 'intervenes amid' MERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver, the liquid metal, is a chemical element (and, for this theme, a planet).

clue.text: Academic poetry is everything

parts.note: uni is short for university, the academic world
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A claim that scholarly poetry is all that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos taken as a whole, all that exists, is everything.

clue.text: Trouble in store tests dress

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A shopper causes a fuss in a shop while checking out a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tests dress' reads as noun-plus-verb, but the definition is a verb phrase: puts clothes on to check fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a garment on to check its fit is a phrasal verb meaning to test clothing.

clue.text: Horse crossing line shown by odd instrument

indicators.note: crossing means the horse goes either side of the line, holding it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A horse stepping over a line is accompanied by some strange tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuned oil-drum of Caribbean bands is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Relatives use it and drop down in a heap

indicators.note: a heap is a jumbled pile, so the letters are thrown together
drop tells us to remove a letter from the word and

explanation.surface: Family members use something and then collapse in a pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop down' takes D from AND, leaving AN; 'in a heap' rearranges USE IT with AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters of one's parents are family members, so relatives.

clue.text: Dave's mate looks for gold boats

parts.note: Sam Moore was Dave Prater's partner in the soul duo Sam and Dave
to pan is to wash gravel in a pan searching for gold

explanation.surface: Dave's friend goes prospecting for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam and Dave were a 1960s American soul duo ('Soul Man').
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-bottomed Chinese skiffs are small boats; plural matches.

clue.text: Colour is of little weight while in prison

indicators.note: in means the small weight is placed inside the prison

parts.note: pent, past participle of the poetic verb pen, means imprisoned or shut up
1 gm, one gram, is a tiny weight, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A colour described as weighing next to nothing when locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of '1 gm' becomes the letter I, a common crossword trick; Chambers allows pent as 'imprisoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that gives paint or skin its tint is a colouring matter, so a colour.

clue.text: One unit in a space probe

indicators.note: in puts the numbers inside the word for a

parts.note: per means a, as in twice a day or twice per day
I is the Roman numeral one
one is the unit, the first whole number

explanation.surface: A single component inside a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like a throwaway article but gives PER, as in 'two tablets per day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American unmanned spacecraft series launched to explore the planets is a famous space probe.

clue.text: Cutter put back in wicker basket

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blade returned to its wicker basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved cavalry sword is a cutting weapon, hence a cutter.

clue.text: Reverse echo misses right note

indicators.note: misses means a letter is left out
reverse says the word for echo is read backwards

parts.note: reverb, reverberation, is an echo effect

explanation.surface: A backwards echo fails to hit the correct note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' turns REVERB into BREVER; 'misses right' drops its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A long note equal to two semibreves in musical notation; a kind of note.

clue.text: Dance performed by Alan Bean and Pete Conrad

definitions.meaning: the gliding backwards step made famous by Michael Jackson

definitions.text: performed by Alan Bean and Pete Conrad
definitions.meaning: the two Apollo 12 astronauts walked on the lunar surface in 1969

explanation.surface: A dance routine credited to two astronauts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Jackson dance move and an astronaut's stroll on the lunar surface go by this name.

clue.text: Extend directions for preserving fish

indicators.note: preserving means the directions keep the fish safe inside them

parts.note: W and N are the compass points west and north
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Broaden the instructions on how to cure fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden or make larger is to extend; a synonym.

clue.text: One going to be equal

definitions.meaning: a humorous coinage: someone who goes to the toilet, one who pees
someone of the same standing or rank as another

explanation.surface: Someone leaving to become an equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' here is the toilet sense, so 'One going' is a jokey noun for someone urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of equal standing, as in being judged by a jury of one's equals, shares the word.

clue.text: Limit velocity returning to Earth from out here

indicators.note: returning means the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit
speed is velocity

explanation.surface: Capping speed on the way back to Earth from the far reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CAPSPEED into DEEPSPAC; E is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: The far regions beyond the solar system are spoken of as being way out here by a distant traveller.

clue.text: Good to stop awful song

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the letter goes inside as a stopper

parts.note: dire means awful

explanation.surface: Something good is needed to halt a dreadful song.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful lament sung at a funeral is a song.

clue.text: Man showing artist round 11

definitions.note: the cross-reference to 11 across, whose answer names an orbiting body

indicators.note: round means the artist goes around the man

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man showing an artist around.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' borrows the answer to 11 across as its definition: Rhea is a moon of Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn's second-largest moon orbits that planet, making it the kind of body named at 11.

clue.text: One watching Sky on stream or off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A TV viewer watching satellite channels, whether or not the stream is running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' suggests the British satellite TV service, but it is the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who observes the stars and planets studies the heavens.
